text: She was one of those. <break time="0.8s" /> Pretty and charming girls. <break time="0.8s" /> Who are sometimes born. <break time="0.8s" /> As if by a mistake of fate. <break time="0.8s" /> Into a family of clerks. <break time="0.8s" /> She had no dowry. <break time="0.8s" /> No hopes. <break time="0.8s" /> And no way. <break time="0.8s" /> Of being known and loved. <break time="0.8s" /> By a rich and important man. <break time="0.8s" /> So she let herself. <break time="0.8s" /> Be married. <break time="0.8s" /> To a minor clerk. <break time="0.8s" /> In the Ministry of Education. <break time="0.8s" /> She suffered endlessly. <break time="0.8s" /> Feeling that she had been born. <break time="0.8s" /> For every luxury and delicacy. <break time="0.8s" /> She suffered from the poorness of her home. <break time="0.8s" /> From its worn walls. <break time="0.8s" /> Its ugly chairs. <break time="0.8s" /> And its faded curtains. <break time="0.8s" /> When she sat down to dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> And her husband cried happily. <break time="0.8s" /> Ah, good soup. <break time="0.8s" /> She dreamed of silver dishes. <break time="0.8s" /> And elegant dinners. <break time="0.8s" /> She had no fine dresses. <break time="0.8s" /> No jewels, nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> And yet she loved. <break time="0.8s" /> Nothing else. <break time="0.8s" /> She had a rich friend. <break time="0.8s" /> A former schoolmate. <break time="0.8s" /> Whom she no longer wanted to visit. <break time="0.8s" /> She suffered so much. <break time="0.8s" /> When she came home. <break time="0.8s" /> From her visits. <break time="0.8s" /> That she cried for days.
